headline: Manchester police arrest man in Moka Pot hate-vandalism case
dek: Tyler Inman, 20, faces criminal mischief and falsifying-evidence charges after police say swastikas and white-power graffiti were left at the downtown coffee shop.
body: Manchester police arrested Tyler Inman, 20, of Allenstown, on Thursday in connection with the vandalism of The Moka Pot coffee shop, according to New Hampshire Public Radio. Inman faces charges of criminal mischief and falsifying evidence.

Police were called to the downtown business on Sept. 16 after several windows were smashed and swastikas and the words “white power” were spray-painted on the building. Investigators said the graffiti appeared intended to intimidate, and they established probable cause for an arrest warrant after reviewing the case.

The New Hampshire Department of Justice said its Civil Rights Unit would take over prosecution because of the serious nature of the allegations. The case remains an accusation, and the charges have not been resolved in court.

Manchester Police Chief Peter Marr described the graffiti as deeply disturbing and said hate has no place in the city. Moka Pot co-owner Nick Carnes has described the cafe as a community gathering space, while Mayor Jay Ruais thanked investigators and said the vandalism did not reflect Manchester’s character.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Manchester Police Arrest Man in Moka Pot Vandalism Case
seoDescription: Manchester police arrested a 20-year-old Allenstown man after hateful graffiti and broken windows were reported at The Moka Pot coffee shop.
